title: PNP preparing for the 'worst' ahead of Sara Duterte impeachment trial verdict -- Jonvic Remulla
summary: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday urged the Philippine National Police (PNP) to remain impartial and prepare for possible scenarios ahead of the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte"s…

blocks.text: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday urged the Philippine National Police (PNP) to remain impartial and prepare for possible scenarios ahead of the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.
Remulla said the proceedings could trigger heightened emotions among supporters of both sides, stressing the need for police officers to maintain order and prevent possible clashes.
"It gets very emotional... Emotions get very high on both sides," Remulla said in an ambush interview.
Remulla reminded police personnel that their primary responsibility is to serve and protect the public particularly during politically sensitive events.
The PNP should help calm the public and ensure that tensions do not escalate into violence or disorder, according to Remulla.
Asked what scenarios the government was preparing for, Remulla said all possibilities ere being considered.
However, he believes Filipinos have already formed their own judgments on the issues and are ready to accept whatever decision the Senate will eventually reach.
"We always expect the worst. Wala namang (There was no) expect the best dito sa (here in) PNP. We always anticipate, we always prepare," he said.
He reiterated that the police force must remain prepared for any eventuality as the impeachment proceedings unfold. — RSJ, GMA News
